title: Petra and the Lantern
premise: In a river-port town of the late colonial era, Jude Oyelaran, indentured to the Meridian Trading Company since his pearl-diver father's death, has survived by being useful and unseen. When seasonal floods close the bridge and the company orders an evacuation with only three berths on the last barge for his family of five, Jude's invisibility shatters: he must bargain with the very merchants who own his debt. Torn between his mother's pride, his sister's ambition, and his forbidden love for the factor's daughter, he uncovers that the berth list was rigged all along to keep him bound. In the end Jude forfeits his own place, forging his father's ledger to free the family — and stays behind as the lanterns go out, only to find that staying was the beginning of his freedom.
about_author: Felix Reyes is the pen name of a former shipping clerk who spent a decade cataloguing port ledgers in West African coastal archives before turning to fiction. He writes about people history recorded only as line items in other men's books.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Jude, POV, introduces his philosophy of measuring life by what can be carried when orders come. He packs the company warehouse at dawn, invisible among crates. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking a lifetime of erasure.

chapters.title: Indenture Papers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback woven through present: how his father's diving debts became Jude's seven-year bond to Meridian. The factor, Mr. Calloway, reminds him two years remain. Beat: resentment banked like coals.

chapters.title: Mother Counts the Rice
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Adaeze, Jude's mother, stretching provisions in the divers' quarter. She refuses charity from the company store, teaching her children what dignity costs. Beat: fierce, fraying love.

chapters.title: The Factor's Daughter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A chance meeting with Miriam Calloway at the lantern market; she buys him a paper lantern as a joke between classes. Their easy talk alarms them both. Beat: first warmth, first fear.

chapters.title: Rain on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Townsperson Elder Bassi's POV. The rains come early; the bridge creaks under floodwater. Rumors spread that the crossing will close within weeks. Beat: dread settling over the town like damp.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Calloway posts the evacuation notice: the last barge leaves before the bridge closes, berths allocated by the company. Jude reads the list twice — his family is on it, barely. Beat: relief with a splinter inside it.

chapters.title: Sister Wants the City
chapters.summary: POV of Ngozi, Jude's sister, who dreams of the capital's schools. She assumes her berth is certain and begins saying goodbyes. Jude says nothing about the fine print. Beat: hope that will need betraying.

chapters.title: Grandfather's River
chapters.summary: Old Tamuno, Jude's grandfather and last of the master divers, takes Jude to the river at night. He speaks of the water taking his son and of debts that outlive men. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, working late in the counting house, he glimpses the true berth allocation: his name is absent; the company means to hold him past the closing. Beat: cold clarity — invisibility was always a cage.

chapters.title: A Lantern Between Us
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. She finds Jude burning the midnight oil and they share stolen conversation about books and escape. She offers to speak to her father. Beat: love offered against duty, both knowing the price.

chapters.title: Calloway's Kindness
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. He genuinely likes Jude but sees only an asset; he dangles a forged extension of 'good standing' to keep him compliant. Beat: corruption wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Berth Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Family council at Adaeze's table: five people, four berths after the company strikes Jude. Who goes? Ngozi must go; Grandfather refuses to leave the river. Beat: love turned into arithmetic, everyone bleeding.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Packing the house, she discards her wedding chest last of all. Jude watches his mother choose what survives her. Beat: grief measured in objects left behind.

chapters.title: Bassi's Warning
chapters.summary: Elder Bassi tells Jude the company has done this before — held workers through the flood season, 'lost' some to the water, extended their bonds. Beat: history repeating as threat.

chapters.title: Night Swimming
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He teaches himself his father's diving breath in the flooded shallows, testing whether he could swim the crossing if no barge will take him. Beat: desperation becoming skill.

chapters.title: Miriam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Miriam confronts her father privately; he offers her a choice: accompany the barge to the capital or stay and lose nothing. She realizes even her freedom is a leash. Beat: duty tightening its elegant knot.

chapters.title: The Forged Page
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Alone with the ledgers, he practices his father's mark and Calloway's initials. He doesn't do it yet — but he knows now that he can. Beat: temptation given hands.

chapters.title: Flood Season Opens
chapters.summary: Town chorus chapter: the bridge officially closes; the town contracts to its lantern-lit core. Prices rise, tempers shorten, the barge date approaches. Beat: the world narrowing.

chapters.title: Ngozi Finds Out
chapters.summary: Ngozi discovers Jude's name is off the list and that he knew. Her fury is the sharpest yet — he let her hope while planning his own sacrifice. Beat: love wounded by protection.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Offer
chapters.summary: Tamuno offers to give his berth to Jude, arguing an old man's life is spent. Jude refuses; Adaeze backs him. Beat: the arithmetic of worth, contested across generations.

chapters.title: Calloway's Audit
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. An internal audit approaches; any tampering with ledgers would be found. He suspects nothing yet but tightens the counting house. Beat: walls closing on two conspiracies at once.

chapters.title: The Lantern Market Burns
chapters.summary: A festival lantern ignites the market stalls; in the chaos, Jude pulls Miriam from the smoke. Witnesses see them together. Beat: passion exposed by fire.

chapters.title: Scandal in the Quarter
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. The factor's household buzzes; her engagement to a company heir is announced to quell rumor. She must choose publicly. Beat: love against duty, made explicit.

chapters.title: Jude's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Jude, humiliated and furious, decides to forge the ledger — not to save himself, but to void his bond entirely so no one can be traded for him. Beat: sacrifice sharpened into strategy.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Secret
chapters.summary: Adaeze reveals she has been saving coin for years — enough to buy out one bond, not two. She offers it for Jude; he redirects it toward Ngozi's school fees. Beat: inheritance redefined as choice, not property.

chapters.title: The Counting House at Night
chapters.summary: Tense set-piece: Jude breaks into the counting house during the audit's eve, alters the bond register, and nearly is caught by the night watchman — saved by Miriam's staged distraction. Beat: terror and trust entwined.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says Now
chapters.summary: Morning: the register shows Jude's bond discharged, paid by a 'deceased uncle.' Calloway smells forgery but cannot prove it without exposing his own falsified berth allocations. Beat: mutual blackmail, unspoken.

chapters.title: Calloway's Countermove
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Rather than accuse, he offers Jude everything — freedom, wages, even a berth — if he testifies that Miriam helped him. Beat: power corrupting into cruelty.

chapters.title: Miriam Chooses
chapters.summary: Miriam publicly breaks her engagement and confesses her part to the company board, gambling that scandal will force them to let the matter die quietly. Beat: duty inverted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Last Barge
chapters.summary: Loading day. Four berths, four travelers: Adaeze, Ngozi, Tamuno — and, at the last moment, Jude's freed name added by the board to bury the scandal. Beat: salvation arriving wrapped in shame.

chapters.title: Goodbye on the Water
chapters.summary: The family embarks; Adaeze presses her wedding chest's single surviving item — her father's diving weight — into Jude's hands. Beat: blessing without permission to grieve.

chapters.title: Alone with the Lantern
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, the town emptying around him. He lights the paper lantern Miriam bought him and lets the river take it. Beat: mourning as release.

chapters.title: The Flood Comes
chapters.summary: The flood peaks; the lower quarter drowns. Jude, using his grandfather's taught breath, dives to save the company's drowned records — and finds evidence of decades of rigged bonds. Beat: the water gives back truth.

chapters.title: Evidence in the Mud
chapters.summary: Jude brings the waterlogged registers to Elder Bassi and the remaining townsfolk. Together they decide: not revenge, but record. Beat: power met with memory.

chapters.title: Calloway Unbound
chapters.summary: Confrontation: Jude presents the drowned ledgers to the arriving board inspector. Calloway's empire of small corruptions collapses; he leaves on the same kind of barge he once rationed. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Miriam Stays
chapters.summary: Miriam, disowned but free, chooses to remain and run the company's local office honestly. She and Jude begin again, this time without secrets. Beat: love rebuilt on level ground.

chapters.title: Letters Across the Water
chapters.summary: Epistolary chapter: letters from Adaeze and Ngozi arrive — school, work, a new city. They send money home for the first time. Beat: inheritance flowing the other way.

chapters.title: The Bridge Reopens
chapters.summary: Dry season; the bridge reopens and the town floods back in. Jude walks it end to end, carrying nothing, weighed by nothing. Beat: freedom as lightness.

chapters.title: Master of His Own Weight
chapters.summary: Jude apprentices formally under no one, reopening his father's diving trade on fair terms, hiring those the company discarded. Beat: inheritance claimed, transformed.

chapters.title: Petra and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Jude's POV, years later: he names his first boat Petra — stone that holds — and hangs a paper lantern at its bow each flood season. The story closes on the river carrying light instead of debt. Beat: peace earned, not given.
